“New” constructions

Specific constructions, their known ingredients, and the proofs that identify their census rings.

What does “new” mean here?

“New” means that, to our knowledge, the specific construction has not been explicitly described in the literature. We do not claim that the resulting category is new up to tensor equivalence or exotic.

R6_4_249Rank 6Multiplicity 4

Sign-swap equivariantization

Condense the diagonal central boson in the product of two identical half-E₆ categories, then equivariantize the factor-swap action with a sign on the condensed algebra.

Ingredients and context. The half-E₆ category; condensation of the diagonal central boson and equivariantization.

Take the category of modules over the diagonal central boson in the product of half-E₆ and PSU(2)₆.

Ingredients and context. The known half-E₆ and PSU(2)₆ categories and their central fermions.

R7_4_35Rank 7Multiplicity 4

Inversion descent from NG(C₄ × C₄, 16)

Construct a near-group orbifold, descend a coherent inversion action, and take the Morita dual associated to the reflection algebra. The resulting invertible group is C₂ × C₂.

Ingredients and context. The Yu–Zhang near-group category NG(C₄ × C₄, 16) and near-group orbifold machinery.

Complete case record →Construction proof ↗

R7_4_2665Rank 7Multiplicity 4

Inversion descent from NG(C₁₆, 16)

Apply the orbifold, inversion-descent and reflection-algebra Morita construction to the cyclic near-group input. Here the invertible group is C₄, and the two large noninvertible simples are mutually dual.

Ingredients and context. Budinski’s NG(C₁₆, 16) category and Izumi’s near-group orbifold machinery.

Complete case record →Construction proof ↗

R8_2_37Rank 8Multiplicity 2

Nonsplit C₂-extension of 2D2

Transport an odd automorphism through a crossed product to obtain an extension in which the odd invertible a satisfies a² = g, with g the nontrivial invertible in the neutral 2D2 category.

Ingredients and context. The known unitary 2D2 category and the Grossman–Izumi–Snyder construction framework.

Complete case record →Construction proof ↗

R8_2_575Rank 8Multiplicity 2

Davydov–Runkel extension of a 16-dimensional Hopf algebra

Use an explicit Davydov–Runkel extension of Kashina’s self-dual 16-dimensional Hopf algebra. The resulting simple dimensions are 1, 1, 1, 1, 2, 2, 2, 4.

Ingredients and context. Kashina’s Hopf algebra and the general Davydov–Runkel extension construction.

Complete case record →Construction proof ↗

Cyclic permutation of three Fibonacci factors

Equivariantize Fib ⊠ Fib ⊠ Fib by the canonical C₃ action that cyclically permutes its factors. Character averaging on the fusion spaces determines the complete tensor.

R9_2_746Rank 9Multiplicity 2

Cyclic generalized TY orbifold · identity coherence

An explicit central C₃ condensation produces a generalized Tambara–Yamagami category with invertible group C₉. Equivariantize its inversion action with the identity square coherence.

Ingredients and context. TY(C₃), a specified pointed C₉ category, and central condensation. R9_2_1209 is the other parity-coherence variant.

Complete case record →Construction proof · identity-coherence variant ↗

R9_2_1209Rank 9Multiplicity 2

Cyclic generalized TY orbifold · parity coherence

Use the same central C₃ condensation and coherent inversion action, with the negative square coherence on the odd component. This yields the second cyclic generalized Tambara–Yamagami orbifold.

Ingredients and context. The same TY(C₃) and pointed C₉ inputs as R9_2_746; the parity natural automorphism changes the coherence.

R9_2_1254Rank 9Multiplicity 2

Order-four descent to a Moore–Read equivariantization

A mixed order-four tensor functor on a covering category descends, after central boson condensation, to a coherent C₂ action on a generalized Moore–Read category. Equivariantization gives the recorded rank-nine model.

Ingredients and context. An Ising category, a specified pointed C₁₆ category, and the generalized Moore–Read construction.

Complete case record →Construction proof and coherent descent ↗

Dihedral pullback of the LPR-24 action · C₃ × C₃
